newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar exchange rates have normalised - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Dollar exchange rates have normalised - Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday that he believed a normalisation process had taken place on the dollar's exchange rate levels compared to those seen in previous years.
"I remain of the opinion that a normalisation has taken place (on the dollar exchange rate)," Waigel said as he arrived in Berlin for Saturday's G7 meeting.
"At the same time, compared with the levels we saw in 1993 and 1994 this is scarcely a change."
The dollar had dropped to historic lows in the spring of 1995. On Friday it stood at 1.66 marks.

Asked whether currency exchange rates would be a priority topic for Saturday's talks, Waigel said: "Every time we meet in this manner we discuss this topic. After all, it is for us to set the agenda."

Earlier this evening, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said in Washington that he expected foreign exchange issues to be a "principal topic" of discussion at the G7 meeting of economic policymakers.
The G7 of seven countries is made up of Germany, Britain, France, Canada, Italy, Japan and the United States.
